mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for an A200 petrol typically costs between £600 and £3,800 depending on the engine code and condition. Used M270 units start from £600-£1,500, reconditioned from £1,500-£2,800, and fully rebuilt M282 engines from £2,200-£3,800. Labour for supply & fit adds £400-£800.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 petrol have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: All A200 petrol engines use timing chains, not belts. The M270 (W176) and M282 (W177) both have timing chains designed to last the life of the engine with proper maintenance. However, the M270 is known for timing chain stretch on higher-mileage units - a metallic rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: On M270-equipped A200 petrol models (W176, 2012-2018), the most common symptom is a metallic rattling noise from the engine on cold start. Other signs include loss of power, rough idle, hesitation, and the engine management light illuminating. If you hear any unusual sounds, have the timing system inspected immediately - ignoring the rattle can lead to catastrophic engine failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A W176 A200 petrol is typically worth £4,000-£14,000 - a rebuilt M270 engine (£1,600-£3,200) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. A W177 A200 petrol is worth £10,000-£22,000 - a rebuilt M282 engine (£2,200-£3,800) is usually well within the car's value. Always compare the cost of repair against the car's market value.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M270 and M282 engines in the A200 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M270 is Mercedes' own 1.6-litre turbo petrol engine used in the W176 A200 (2012-2018), producing 156 hp with a timing chain. The M282 is a 1.3-litre turbo petrol engine co-developed with the Renault-Nissan Alliance, used in the W177 A200 (2018-present), producing 163 hp. The M282 features Nanoslide cylinder coating technology and, in later models, 48V mild-hybrid assistance.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 petrol to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the A200 petrol can be caused by several issues depending on the engine. On M270 engines, timing chain stretch can cause cam timing drift, reducing power. On both M270 and M282, carbon buildup on intake valves from direct injection can restrict airflow. On M282 engines, water pump or thermostat failure can cause overheating and subsequent power reduction.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The A200 petrol badge arrived with the third-generation W176 A-Class in 2012, positioned as the mid-range petrol option above the A180. It introduced Mercedes' new M270 1.6-litre turbocharged engine, replacing the older naturally aspirated M266 units. The badge continued into the W177 generation in 2018 with the co-developed M282 1.3-litre turbo engine, which later gained 48V mild-hybrid assistance from 2020.

milestones.description: M270.920, 1.6L turbo petrol, 156 hp (115 kW) - W176 A200 launch; direct injection, timing chain, 250 Nm torque; 7G-DCT or 6-speed manual
Facelift with revised engine management; power remains 156 hp; emissions improved to Euro 6
M282.914, 1.3L turbo petrol, 163 hp (120 kW) - W177 A200 launch; co-developed with Renault-Nissan Alliance; 7G-DCT standard
M282.914 gains 48V mild-hybrid assistance; +13 hp electric boost; 8G-DCT introduced
Facelift with M282.914 continuing; 48V mild-hybrid now standard across all A200 petrol models

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 petrol is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The A200 petrol has been powered by two distinct turbocharged engines across its production life - the M270 1.6-litre (W176) and the co-developed M282 1.3-litre (W177). Each has distinct failure patterns. Rebuilt A200 petrol engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M270 Timing Chain Stretch - Why the W176 A200 Petrol Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The M270 turbo petrol engine's timing chain can stretch prematurely, causing a metallic rattling noise when starting from cold. The chain tensioner can also fail, allowing the chain to skip timing. Post-2014 models have strengthened timing components, making failure less common but not eliminated.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Best done at first rattle; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M270 with upgraded timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped; bent valves almost certain

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W176 A200 petrol is worth £4,000-£14,000 depending on condition and mileage. For vehicles under £5,000, a preventative chain replacement (£1,200-£1,800) is usually the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For higher-value examples, a rebuilt M270 with warranty (£1,600-£3,200) offers peace of mind.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the engine on cold starts - especially between 80,000 and 120,000 miles - act immediately. A preventative chain replacement at a specialist saves thousands compared to waiting for failure. Once the chain jumps, piston-to-valve contact is almost certain and engine replacement becomes the only viable option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M270 Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 petrol engine prices

problems.h4: M282 Water Pump & Thermostat Failure - W177 A200 Petrol Cooling System Issues
problems.rootCause: The M282 engine is prone to water pump and thermostat failures, leading to coolant leaks and overheating. This is a known weakness of the co-developed Renault-Nissan engine architecture, with the plastic housing being particularly susceptible to cracking.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, flush coolant system
Complete engine with upgraded cooling components
repairOptions.longevity: Only if overheating has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: If you notice coolant leaks, overheating, or the temperature gauge fluctuating, have the cooling system inspected immediately. A £350-£650 specialist water pump replacement is far cheaper than a £2,200 engine replacement.

problems.group: M270 & M282 Intake Valve Carbon Buildup
problems.h4: M270 & M282 Intake Valve Carbon Buildup - Direct Injection Deposits
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz A-Class 200 petrol (M270.920 and M282.914, W176 and W177, 2012-present)
problems.rootCause: Direct injection engines like the M270 and M282 suffer from carbon buildup on intake valves because fuel is injected directly into the cylinder rather than washing over the valves. This is especially problematic on vehicles driven predominantly in the city.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove intake manifold, blast valves with walnut media
repairOptions.longevity: Viable; restores performance and fuel economy

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with cleaned intake system
repairOptions.longevity: Only if carbon buildup has caused significant valve damage

problems.recommendation: If your A200 petrol feels sluggish or has reduced fuel economy, carbon cleaning is often the solution. Regular motorway driving helps reduce carbon buildup. A £350-£600 specialist clean is far cheaper than a £1,600 engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for M270 and M282 carbon cleaning and engine replacement for your A200 petrol
